correctness.rationale: The ordered pair at step i is (x_{i-1},x_i); overlap with the next pair reconstructs the indexed input from a closed path with specified starting site. Closing the path enforces the repeated slots even for 1 and 2 sites; no rotation multiplier enters. The trace therefore counts the full fiber. Capping each nonnegative entry at two commutes with capped multiplication and preserves whether the sum on the diagonal is one. In a separate endpoint-set encoding I generated all 476 states, with 136 accepting, and checked the denominator product, the recurrence vector at exponent 21 in every state, and the full numerator through degree 20. Multiplication by further powers of the transition matrix yields the recurrence for every n>=21; it is not inferred from the observed sequence. Exhaustive direct counts at n=1,...,12 also agreed, as did the transfer counts through n=16.
residual_risks: The independent direct enumeration is bounded; the finite whole-vector identity and closed-path bijection prove the all-length formal series. No multistep or rotation-quotiented count is proven.

value.rationale: Unique reconstruction from one observed cyclic configuration is a natural refinement of image enumeration for this classical majority rule. The exact rational series resolves every indexed ring size, and distinguishes the count of outputs that carry enough information to recover the input even when the total image count alone is known. The exact recurrence makes the refinement usable at lengths beyond direct enumeration.
residual_risks: The result is specific to one update and one fiber size, rather than a full inverse distribution or a claim that the finite-state method is new.
